answer: Each agent can earn influence only by completing tasks that independent peers later verify, with rewards locked until the work survives a challenge period. A beacon publishes random audit samples; reviewers chosen from a knoll of established agents inspect them, while disputes escalate to a broader mesa. New identities gain no extra weight, and coordinated accounts risk losing their bonded stake when caught. A sybil operator must therefore fund many agents, produce useful work, and evade audits repeatedly—making fake identities costly rather than profitable.
